explanations.text: Priya reviews your Docker and PyTorch work, so you learn from someone a step ahead.
Tom reviews your SQL; you pair up on the project and learn by doing.
You review Mei's Python; teaching it is the fastest way to lock it in.

project.title: VisionAid: accessible image captioning API
project.pitch: A small open-source API that writes alt text for images, so blind and low-vision users get useful descriptions on any website. Each of you builds the part you want to learn, and a podmate who already knows it reviews your pull request.
milestones: Week 1: Captioning API runs in Docker
Week 2: Fine-tuned model with quality checks

issues.title: Containerise the captioning API with Docker
issues.body:
Package the FastAPI captioning service so anyone in the pod can run it with one command.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A `Dockerfile` builds the API on a slim Python base image
- [ ] `docker compose up` starts the API on port 8000
- [ ] `GET /health` returns `{"status":"ok"}` inside the container
- [ ] The README has a "Run with Docker" section

**Learning focus:** Docker · **Reviewer:** Priya (teaches Docker)
issues.milestone: Week 1: Captioning API runs in Docker

issues.title: Design the Postgres schema for caption requests
issues.body:
Store every caption request so the pod can measure quality and latency later.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A `requests` table with id, image_url, caption, model_version, latency_ms and created_at
- [ ] A migration script in `db/migrations/`
- [ ] One SQL query that returns the 10 slowest requests this week
- [ ] Indexes are explained in a short comment

**Learning focus:** SQL · **Reviewer:** Tom (teaches SQL)
issues.milestone: Week 1: Captioning API runs in Docker

issues.title: Write the Python image preprocessing module
issues.body:
Resize and normalise uploaded images before they reach the model.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `preprocess.py` exposes `load_image(path) -> Tensor`
- [ ] Images are resized to 384×384 and keep their aspect ratio with padding
- [ ] Corrupt or non-image files raise a clear `ValueError`
- [ ] Three pytest tests cover the happy path and both error cases

**Learning focus:** Python · **Reviewer:** Aisha (teaches Python)
issues.milestone: Week 1: Captioning API runs in Docker

issues.title: Fine-tune a small captioning model in PyTorch
issues.body:
Fine-tune a pretrained image-captioning model on a small accessibility-focused dataset.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A training script in `model/train.py` that runs on a laptop CPU in under 20 minutes on the sample set
- [ ] Training loss is logged every 50 steps
- [ ] The best checkpoint is saved to `model/checkpoints/`
- [ ] A short note on what you changed and why

**Learning focus:** PyTorch · **Reviewer:** Priya (teaches PyTorch)
issues.milestone: Week 2: Fine-tuned model with quality checks

issues.title: Add PyTorch batch inference and a caption quality check
issues.body:
Caption a folder of test images in batches and flag captions that are too vague to be useful as alt text.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `model/infer.py` captions a folder of images in batches of 8
- [ ] Captions shorter than 4 words or containing "image of" are flagged
- [ ] Results are written to `reports/quality.csv`
- [ ] Inference runs under `torch.no_grad()`

**Learning focus:** PyTorch · **Reviewer:** Priya (teaches PyTorch)
issues.milestone: Week 2: Fine-tuned model with quality checks

issues.title: Build the React upload page with screen-reader support
issues.body:
A simple page where a user uploads an image and hears the generated caption.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Drag-and-drop and a keyboard-accessible file button
- [ ] The caption is announced through an `aria-live` region
- [ ] Loading and error states are visible and announced
- [ ] The page passes an axe check with no serious issues

**Learning focus:** React · **Reviewer:** Mei (teaches React)

issues.title: Deploy the API to AWS
issues.body:
Put VisionAid online so the pod can demo it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The Docker image is pushed to ECR
- [ ] The API runs on ECS Fargate or App Runner behind HTTPS
- [ ] Uploaded images are stored in a private S3 bucket with a 7-day lifecycle rule
- [ ] The README lists the monthly cost estimate (free tier where possible)

**Learning focus:** AWS · **Reviewer:** Tom (teaches AWS)
